entities.summary:
Bartolino da Novara (fl. 1370s) was an Italian military architect and engineer who designed fortifications and infrastructure for the Republic of Venice.

Born in Novara, Italy, around 1360, Bartolino rose to prominence as a military engineer during the Venetian-Miscianine War. He designed and implemented various fortifications, including the Castello di Malcontenta, and worked on the construction of the Grand Canal's eastern embankment.

His most notable work, however, was the design and construction of the fortifications for the Republic of Venice's expansion into the Adriatic region. He also worked on the renovation of the city's defenses and infrastructure.

Bartolino's work had a lasting impact on the development of Venetian engineering and architecture, and his designs continue to be studied by historians and architects today.

One notable quote from Bartolino da Novara is: 'A good engineer must always consider the needs of the client and the location.'

Bartolino da Novara is the subject of the 1981 book 'Bartolino da Novara: Architetto e Ingegnere Militare,' which provides a detailed analysis of his life and work.

Bartolino da Novara's work has been recognized for its significance in the development of Venetian engineering and architecture, and he is considered one of the most important military architects of the Middle Ages.
